meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'held back / held on'.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'статься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke up / parted', paired with 'расставаться'.

examples.text: Вот поэтому он решил с тобой расстаться.
examples.trans: That is why he decided to break up with you.
We will definitely break up.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Странно, а ты откуда всё это знаешь?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знаться'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to confess / admit', paired with 'признаваться'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.
